ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two small particles of equal masses start moving in opposite directions from a point A in a horizontal circular orbit. Their tangential velocities are $v$ and $2v$, respectively, as shown in the figure. Between collisions, the particles move with constant speeds. After making how many elastic collisions, other than that at A, these two particles will again reach the point A?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a horizontal circular track, with point A marked at the top of the circumference. Two small balls start from near A and move in opposite tangential directions along the circumference: the left arrow points to the left and is labeled with speed v, and the right arrow points to the right and is labeled with speed 2v. Reasoning: Let the circumference of the circular track be L. The two particles have equal mass, and when a one-dimensional elastic collision occurs, they exchange velocities; therefore, in order to calculate the position and number of collisions, it can be equivalently regarded as two “shadow particles” passing through each other while their velocities remain unchanged. In this way, one moves in one direction with v, and the other moves in the opposite direction with 2v, so the relative speed is 3v. The times when they meet, that is, when collisions occur, satisfy that the combined distance traveled is an integer multiple of the circumference: t_n = nL/(3v). When n=1, the first meeting is at a position whose distance from A is not zero; when n=2, the second meeting is also not at A; when n=3, t=L/v, at this time the shadow particle with speed v has traveled L, and the shadow particle with speed 2v has traveled 2L, and both return to A. Therefore, before reaching A again, 2 elastic collisions have already occurred outside A.

raw_record.question_text: Two small particles of equal masses start moving in opposite directions from a point A in a horizontal circular orbit. Their tangential velocities are $v$ and $2v$, respectively, as shown in the figure. Between collisions, the particles move with constant speeds. After making how many elastic collisions, other than that at A, will these two particles again reach the point A?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: a circular track has point A at the top, with two particles starting at A and moving tangentially in opposite directions; the left-going particle is labeled v and the right-going particle is labeled 2v. From the text, note that the masses are equal, collisions are elastic, and speeds remain constant between collisions. Let the circumference be L. For a 1D elastic collision between equal masses, the particles exchange velocities, so for counting meeting/collision events we can equivalently pretend they pass through each other unchanged. In this pass-through model, the two ghost particles move oppositely with relative speed 3v and collide whenever their combined traveled distance is an integer multiple of L: t_n = nL/(3v). The third such meeting, n=3, occurs at t=L/v, when the v ghost has gone one full circumference and the 2v ghost has gone two full circumferences, so both are back at A. The earlier meetings n=1 and n=2 are away from A. Therefore, before reaching A again, they have made 2 elastic collisions other than at A.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一条水平圆形轨道，圆周顶部标有点 A。两小球从 A 附近出发，沿圆周切向相反方向运动：左侧箭头指向左方并标注速度 v，右侧箭头指向右方并标注速度 2v。

推理：设圆形轨道周长为 L。两粒子质量相等，发生一维弹性碰撞时会交换速度；因此为了计算碰撞发生的位置和次数，可以等效看作两个“影子粒子”彼此穿过而速度不变。这样，一个以 v 沿一方向运动，另一个以 2v 沿相反方向运动，相对速度为 3v。它们相遇即发生碰撞的时刻满足合走路程为圆周长的整数倍：t_n = nL/(3v)。当 n=1 时，第一次相遇在离 A 不为零的位置；当 n=2 时，第二次相遇也不在 A；当 n=3 时，t=L/v，此时速度为 v 的影子粒子走了 L，速度为 2v 的影子粒子走了 2L，二者都回到 A。因此再次到达 A 之前，在 A 以外已经发生了 2 次弹性碰撞。
